name: Mor (Bomberai Peninsula)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Voorhoeve 1975 classification remarks found via Glottolog; no grammar/phonology of Mor (Bomberai) located

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Mor. New Guinea World (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch, DokuWiki page, last modified 2024-06-25).
sources.note: Second-hand digest of Hammarström (2012) 'sketch grammar for Mor of Goras': pp. 5-9 consonant/vowel inventory (15 or 18 C, 5 V); pp. 11-12 pronouns reproduced with stress marks (ˈna-ja 1SG, ˈa-ja 2SG, mene 3SG, ˈni-a 1PL, ˈi-a 2PL, ˈmire 3PL). Phonology section marked 'under construction'; no statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Moran & McCloy (eds.), PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory UPSID 464 'MOR', source Laycock, Don. 1978. A little Mor. In Wurm & Carrington (eds.), Second International Conference on Austronesian Linguistics: Proceedings, fasc. 1 (PL C-61), 285ff.
sources.note: No tone/stress marked; but this inventory is misassigned: Laycock 1978 describes the Austronesian Mor of Cenderawasih Bay (ISO mhz), not Bomberai Mor. Irrelevant to morb1239.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists. Pacific Linguistics B-31. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-B31.
sources.note: Checklist entry 47 'Mor, stock-level isolate' (+-60 speakers, source Anceaux 1958) and a 40-item comparative wordlist column (after Anceaux); no stress marks and no prosodic remarks.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy & Antoinette Schapper. 2022. The Greater West Bomberai language family. Oceanic Linguistics 61(1): 469-527. doi:10.1353/ol.2021.0028 (HAL open copy of published version).
sources.note: Nothing on Mor stress. Mor appears only as an outcomparison language (fn. 12, p. 484: mene '3SG', míre '3PL', me-, mí-, -me, -mi, cited from Hammarström 2010:10-11, with acute marks carried over) and in the bibliography, which identifies the primary description: 'Hammarström, Harald. 2010. Notes on Mor [moq] of the Bomberai peninsula. Unpublished manuscript.'

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9783110295252-002 (OAPEN open-access chapter via archive.org).
sources.note: Gives a Mor phoneme inventory (p. 87, 'Mor (probable non-TNG isolate)': m n b d g t k ɸ z[ʑ] s r[r,l] w j; i e a o u, from Hammarström fieldnotes 2010) and a note on noun number (sec. 2.5.2.4), but the prosody section 2.4.3 (pp. 88-89) does not mention Mor; no stress statement for Mor.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Sec. 2.4.13 (p. 190) inventories Mor documentation (Anceaux 1958 wordlist; Smits & Voorhoeve 1998; unpublished SIL Indonesia survey Walker 1983; Donohue 2010 200-word list; Anceaux Nachlass KITLV Or. 615). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010 [rev. 2012]. Notes on Mor [moq] of the Bomberai peninsula / sketch grammar of Mor of Goras. Unpublished manuscript (cited by Usher & Schapper 2022 and by Usher, New Guinea World, with phonology on pp. 5-9).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only description of Mor with a phonology section; its transcriptions carry IPA stress marks, so it almost certainly states (or lets one read off) the stress pattern. Obtainable only from the author.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2018. Language isolates in the New Guinea region. In Lyle Campbell (ed.), Language Isolates, 287-322. London: Routledge.

sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Glottolog links this chapter to Mor; the author did the only modern fieldwork on Mor, so its Mor section may summarise phonology including stress.

sources.citation: Smits, Leo & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1998. The J. C. Anceaux collection of wordlists of Irian Jaya languages B: Non-Austronesian (Papuan) languages (Part II). Irian Jaya Source Materials 10. Leiden/Jakarta: DSALCUL/IRIS.

sources.note: Largest published Mor wordlist (Anceaux and de Jong lists); Anceaux-collection transcriptions sometimes carry stress accents, which would give raw evidence of stress position.

sources.citation: Walker, Roland. 1983. SIL Indonesia survey of the Bomberai peninsula (wordlists and some grammatical data on Mor). Unpublished, SIL Indonesia (cited in Hammarström 2010: 190).

sources.note: Unpublished survey with Mor wordlists and grammatical data; SIL survey wordlists are usually stress-marked.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J. C. 1958. Languages of the Bomberai Peninsula: outline of a linguistic map. Nieuw-Guinea Studiën 2: 109-121; and Anceaux Nachlass, KITLV Or. 615 (aanvulling 4-23, Mor wordlists).

sources.note: First report of Mor; the archival wordlists may carry accent marks. Low chance of an explicit stress statement.
